newsitem.title: USA: Dollar ends lower in US, hurt by Rivlin report.
newsitem.headline: Dollar ends lower in US, hurt by Rivlin report.

text.p: The dollar closed lower against the mark and the yen on Friday, hurt by reported comments from Federal Reserve Vice Chair Alice Rivlin, which raised concerns that U.S. administration tolerance for a higher dollar may be limited.
The dollar slumped after a wire service reported that Rivlin had said during a speech in Nebraska on Thursday that U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin had set limits on his strong dollar policy.
When contacted by Reuters on Friday, the Fed denied Rivlin had made the remarks, but the damage had already been done.

"These kinds of comments are not characteristic. The dollar immediately blipped down. And that it came from the Fed, not the Administration. The market takes that quite seriously," said John Nelson, foreign exchange trading manager at ABN AMRO Bank.

In the United States, the dollar closed lower against the mark, settling at 1.6863/68 marks from 1.6914/19 at the open. The dollar also moved lower against the yen, which surged, ending at 122.75/80 yen from 123.20/25.
The comments led investors to question the dollar's upside potential, despite hopes for higher U.S. interest rates.

The dollar had rallied on Thursday as market players, encouraged by comments made by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan, bet that short-term interest rates would be raised at a key policy meeting on Tuesday.

Even before the Rivlin comments sent the dollar lower on Friday, weakness against the yen surfaced after U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshevky warned Japan against trying to export its way out of recesssion.
"Barshevsky said she was not too pleased with the export-led recovery in Japan and would rather see a recovery led by domestic growth," said Lisa Finstrom, a Smith Barney currency analyst.

Her comments reignited quesitons about whether the dollar's strong gains against the yen may be slowing. The greenback has risen about six percent against the yen since the beginning of the year and by over 50 percent from its lows in early 1995.

The yen's early strength also weighed on the dollar. The Japanese currency moved sharply higher against the Swiss franc after Swiss National Bank board member Bruno Gehrig said the central bank would maintain its generous monetary policy.
But some were careful to note that the dollar's weakness came on the heels of Thursday's strong gains.

"After the highs from the night before, naturally we were going to have some consolidation. Especially on a day with so little liquidity. It's Friday, we've got Easter coming and people are hesitating to take big positions ahead of the FOMC meeting," said one foreign exchange trader.
In other trade, the British pound strengthened in the United States, closing at $1.6047/57 from $1.6005/15.
The dollar closed slightly lower against the Swiss franc at 1.4570/80 from its opening at 1.4590/00. It closed just a hair lower against the Canadian dollar, at C$1.3783/88 against C$1.3784/89.
The dollar closed at $0.7865/70 Australian dollars compared to $0.7851/56 at the open.
